sample_unit: orthopedic physicians (27 intermediate, 15 senior) diagnosing 40 rare disease cases

links.outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with versus without LLM assistance (2-stage workflow)
links.effect: Mean accuracy rose from 42.22% to 68.80% (intermediate) and 58.67% to 83.33% (senior); stage significantly associated with correctness (P<.001). Overreliance was not formally assessed.
links.quote: Before LLM assistance, mean physician-level accuracy was 42.22% for intermediate physicians and 58.67% for senior physicians; after assistance, it increased to 68.80% and 83.33%, respectively.

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy when using LLM in workflow versus independent baseline
links.effect: LLM assistance associated with higher diagnostic correctness in both groups (P<.001); case-level accuracy improved from 40% to 67.5% (intermediate) and 57.5% to 82.5% (senior).
links.quote: Secondary case-level analyses using the >50% threshold showed improvement from 40% (16/40) to 67.5% (27/40) for intermediate physicians and from 57.5% (23/40) to 82.5% (33/40) for senior physicians, with similar findings using the ≥2/3 threshold.

links.outcome: LLM primary-diagnosis accuracy on orthopedic rare diseases
links.effect: Claude Sonnet 4.5, ChatGPT-5.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro each 90% (36/40); DeepSeek-V3.2 67.5% (27/40); Cochran Q P<.001.
links.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.5, ChatGPT-5.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro each achieved 90% (36/40) primary-diagnosis accuracy, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 achieved 67.5% (27/40; Cochran Q P<.001).

unlisted_practices: Two-stage LLM-assisted diagnostic workflow for rare disease diagnosis by physicians of different seniority

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates a 2-stage clinical workflow comparing physicians' diagnostic accuracy before and after reviewing LLM recommendations for orthopedic rare diseases.

primary.practice: physician review of LLM diagnostic suggestions in a 2-stage workflow
